full_review_text:
# Independent review: InternalWO and OrderRec

Verdict: the theorem statements and mathematical proofs are clean. The review
found no Choice circularity, external well-foundedness premise, arbitrary
predicate induction, or implicit semantic Separation schema. Three documentation
caveats and concrete application obligations remain below. This was a full
source/API read, with no compiler invocation, no independent axiom-print run,
and no tracked edits.

Reviewed source: commit8735ac3f39, current files byte-identical to that commit.
Snapshots are `/tmp/zfc-order-rec-review-sources/{InternalWO,OrderRec}.lean`;
relevant dependency snapshots are in the same directory. Structured evidence,
Git blob identifiers and declaration lists are `/tmp/zfc-order-rec-review.json`.

## Exact internal semantics and assumptions

`InternalWO.lean:28-33` defines a reflexive total order on a class P and asks
for least elements only for represented sets Z whose members lie in P. This is
not external `WellFounded`, a well-order of every external subclass, a
represented relation set, or a set-likeness assertion for every initial segment.
The class/relation arguments may be external predicates; the explicit resource
hypotheses below are therefore important.

The `H : ZFAxioms mem` bundle is precisely the six-field interface at
`SetTheory/ZF/Lean/ZF/Zf.lean:334-343`: Extensionality, actual-formula
Separation, Pairing, Union, Infinity, actual-formula partial functional
Replacement. It contains no Power, Regularity or Choice. `Regular mem` is the
represented-set minimality property at `InternalOrd.lean:26-27`, which does not
imply external well-foundedness of membership in an arbitrary model.

`wo_nat` (`InternalWO.lean:64`) applies this Regularity to an arbitrary
represented nonempty set of internal naturals, using internal natural-number
linearity. It does not restrict naturals to external standard numerals. An
external descending sequence in a nonstandard model is not automatically a
represented set, so its existence does not contradict the theorem.

The restriction and relation-congruence lemmas preserve exactly this internal
semantics. `wo_lex` (`InternalWO.lean:139`) separates only pair projections and
fibers using formulas for pair membership; it does not demand Separation for
P1, P2, r1 or r2. Both projections are bounded by double Union of the represented
set of pairs (`comp_mem_uu`, `firsts_exists`, `fibre_exists`, lines90-118).
Lexicographic leastness selects a least first coordinate and then a least
second-coordinate fiber. No Choice function over all fibers is chosen.

`wo_pull` explicitly assumes `hset` (`InternalWO.lean:199-215`): for each
represented set of PY-elements there is a represented set of ALL their keys.
In particular every single-element key fiber must be set-sized internally.
The proof applies hset first to a singleton, finds a least key by hK, and uses
key uniqueness to prove antisymmetry. Its all-key comparison relation is valid;
it does not silently assume a chosen global least-key function.

This hset is a real remaining resource. For example, in ordinary ZF let PY
contain only the empty set, PK be all ordinals, and give that sole element every
ordinal as a key. Nonempty key fibers, unique decoding of a key and the internal
ordinal order do not produce a set of all keys of that singleton. A concrete
constructible-order application must bound key levels or use another bounded
key presentation; arbitrary stage/formula keys cannot be collected for free.

`wo_append` assumes `hsep` (`InternalWO.lean:242-244`) for PA. It does not infer
Separation for every external predicate. The actual `step_wos` application
supplies that resource by the literal formula `pmemF 1 0 0` for the old field
(`OrderRec.lean:142-149`). `prod_exists` separately assumes a Power-set interface
and applies it twice (`InternalWO.lean:294-307`); Power is not hidden in H.

## Recursion and named formulas

`OrderRec.lean:119-123` packages four explicit append-operation obligations:
exact pair-edge decomposition, old/new disjointness, an internal well-order on
the new block, and endpoint coverage for its order edges. `step_wos` proves the
old/new ordered sum and exact end-extension. A future application must prove
these hypotheses. In particular `AppendOp.wo` cannot be discharged by assuming
that every arbitrary new set can be well-ordered in a Choice-free argument.

`stage_wos` (`OrderRec.lean:189-205`) additionally requires Regularity and a
`TransRec.DefOp` witness. `DefOp` (`TransRec.lean:28-30`) is a genuine named-formula
graph adapter, whose satisfaction theorem holds for every environment and every
choice of input/output names. It is not a promise of closure for an arbitrary
external operation. N and O need no graph adapters in this generic theorem:
they occur in its explicit semantic append resource, while the actual induction
predicate mentions G through D.gF and is internally definable.

`isWOSF w` uses fresh names w+1,w+2,w+3 (`OrderRec.lean:79-96`), including a
represented-set quantifier for leastness. `endExtF a b` chooses a+b+1 and its
successor (`lines99-110`), so it works even when a=b. Pair-membership helpers
introduce still-fresh local names (`InternalRank.lean:40-45,76-82`). The stage
induction formula keeps name0 for the ordinal, name1 for W, names2/3 for c/Wc,
and name4 for G(Wc); the named satisfaction proof matches the target property.
Locally reused names in separate conjuncts or antecedents do not capture those
parameters.

The induction is `InternalOrd.ord_induction` (`lines96-116`), which cuts a set
of named-formula counterexamples inside the successor of the target ordinal.
Thus the property applies to every internal ordinal, including nonstandard
ones, with no unrestricted semantic induction principle.

At a union stage, pair edges and fields lie in images of earlier stages by
`stage_spec`. Comparability and exact end-extension give a common upper image
for any two such images (`OrderRec.lean:216-252`). For leastness, choose any
member of the represented test set, take a stage containing it, separate the
test set by that stage's field using `pmemF 1 0 0`, and choose its least member
there (`lines277-293`). Every point outside that field lies above it in a later
image. This uses no collection of stages indexed by all test-set elements and
no Choice of a witness stage for every element.

Imported selected set constructors are metatheoretic noncomputable choices of
witnesses guaranteed by the six model axioms. That does not add an object-level
Axiom of Choice to these statements. The reviewed modules introduce no custom
axiom or admission.

## Documentation caveats and remaining applications

1. `InternalWO.lean:15-17` says the canonical constructible well-order is assembled
   in ConstructibleOrder; `OrderRec.lean:15-17` similarly names CodeOrder and
   ConstructibleOrder. Neither module exists in the reviewed checkout. These
   are intended applications, not current conclusions, and should be described
   in future tense until supplied.
2. The header `OrderRec.lean:6` describes W as a set of Kuratowski pairs.
   `IsWOS` actually constrains only `Le W x y := mem (kpair x y) W`
   (`lines31-44`). It permits nonpair junk. In an ordinary ZF model,
   W={emptyset} has an empty coded field and satisfies these conditions while
   containing a nonpair. This causes no error in the Le/Fld/stage_wos proofs.
   If a later object-level well-order relation requires all members to be
   pairs, supply that condition or separate the pair-coded members of W;
   this tidying preserves Le and Fld.
3. Concrete code/constructible order operators, their all-environment DefOp
   formulas and all four AppendOp properties still need construction. Any
   least-key application needs explicit set bounds for all keys of a
   represented family. Ordering only external standard formula codes does not
   cover the complete internal/nonstandard code domain. A named internal
   choice-function construction from the resulting concrete order is also
   separate. These modules themselves conclude no ConstructibleOrder theorem,
   Choice axiom, ZFC model, machine calibration or PA-provable translation.

The existing constructible hierarchy/absoluteness files are useful dependencies;
these two new generic kits do not by themselves close that final comparison.
followup: Only module headers were clarified after this read-only review; the exact current sources were freshly checked in the160-unit integration. No theorem body changed.
